subtitle: The four recomposed core experiences of the public homepage after the founder approved the visual direction and asked for one finishing pass: the finished state recorded from the final code, Astra's final verification of that state, the scores before to after, and the measured performance. Nothing is migrated.
status: Lab only. The founder approved the visual direction (dark, spatial, glass and material language, motion concept) on the recomposition package and asked for one focused finishing pass on the four experiences. That pass is done and stopped: hero hierarchy, Recreate continuity, Drive integration, the Loyalty close, material refinement, a phone pass at 390px and media weight. The V3 product architecture is unchanged: the same routes, fixtures, amounts, dates, truth rules, Loyalty model, preview entrances, Pause motion and reduced motion. Story, Get paid, Find people, Find cars, Create, Review, Monthly content, User Home, Profile, Business Home and the Loyalty app screens were not touched. Waiting for the founder's approval before any further screen.
kept_and_changed: Kept: one account, two modes, both audiences on one page through ?audience=earn|business, the Menu anchors, Sign in and every preview entrance (Open preview, View campaign, View person, Request, Open loyalty preview), the lab entrance and Pause motion, ordered stationary states under reduced motion, keyboard steps.

Kept: every media binding in docs/design-lab-v3/MEDIA_MANIFEST.json. The reference stays Loopday's US$75 on approval opportunity; Counter pour stays Maya's own version approved Sep 10, 2026 with no ledger record; Latte take stays a separate recorded example under Get paid; Eli's US$240 asking rate stays separate from the Spurroom Bikes US$300 /month campaign; Jasmine stays a typographic source with no portrait; the loyalty preview keeps its 10, 6, 1, 2 baseline.

Changed: the four experiences are pinned scenes driven by native scroll on desktop and tablet (no wheel interception, no snapping), stepped compositions in ordinary flow on phone, and stationary blocks per beat under reduced motion. One engine (src/app/design-lab-v3/x/Film.tsx) writes transform, opacity and clip to persistent elements once per animation frame.

Changed: the navigation is the one persistent lens, dark over the hero substrate and light over the inspection substrate, 1200px maximum on desktop, with the lab and motion band beneath it. The hero substrate is #171B1D and the inspection substrate #E8ECEB, per the director's material system.

Added: one generated lab photograph, the oxblood estate wagon, briefed by the director, rendered by the final image model and approved by the director after four rounds across three runs (scores 9, 9, 9, 9). It is an illustrative vehicle example bound to nothing but the public Drive and hero glimpse; vehicle-eli-01 keeps its listing, campaign example and proof bindings everywhere else.
Not built, per the direction: no Smart Vehicle concept, no generated creator, customer or cafe imagery, no new Story workflow, no counterfeit earned amount, no idle animation.

The finishing pass touched only the film engine, the three scene files and their styles, the media helpers and derivatives, the late image component, the director's verify job and the package tooling. The exact file list is in the last section.

experiences.title: Public hero
experiences.body: Two audience lines are the controls. The Loopday reference is the foreground anchor of a composition of real, unequal product objects on the dark substrate: Maya's portrait, the Story creative, the vehicle example, Loopday's own business photograph, the coded program object and the opportunity terms attached to the reference's lower edge. In the business lens Maya's own Counter pour joins her portrait, the reference is labelled Campaign reference and the attached sheet carries her name with View person and Request. Over the first 240px of desktop scroll the supporting planes converge behind the advancing reference and are occluded before they leave, the terms retract beneath its edge, and the same reference arrives on the inspection stage as the Recreate reference. On phone the handoff runs in the flow slot through Explore earning and the sequence controls.

experiences.after_pass_2: Terms text area kept clear of the reference (Loopday Coffee above US$75, Maya Chen fully exposed in the business lens); the navigation sits dark over the hero substrate and exchanges its backing only when the inspection substrate reaches it; the audience lines leave with the substrate so no white type sits on the light stage in reverse; the business sheet sits in contact with Maya's portrait and work on desktop.
experiences.truth: Words in the hero besides navigation, actions and lab controls: Make money, Grow your business, Recreate (Campaign reference in the business lens), Loopday Coffee, US$75, On approval, Vehicle example, Loyalty, Take a coffee break. (the Story's own lettering), Maya Chen (business lens). The amount is the reference opportunity's conditional term. Nothing implies Maya made the reference or accepted the opportunity.
experiences.finishing: One focal object. The reference and its attached terms are the only full contrast plane; the creator and the Story rest one tier back, the vehicle and the program object a tier further with a touch of depth of field, and Loopday's own photograph is the far context, dim and soft. The inactive audience line is brighter and has a focus ring. The phone hero is composed for 390px rather than compressed from the desktop: a 268px reference with the terms attached beneath it, the creator beside it, the Story peeking behind its corner and the vehicle as a glimpse; the business photograph, the program object and the vehicle label are not part of the phone composition and the photograph is never requested there.

experiences.title: Recreate sequence
experiences.body: One carrier changes custody and state four times. Reference: the hero's reference in inspection position with its terms. Creator version: a hard vertical boundary (draggable, keyboard operable) wipes Loopday's reference away over Maya's registered version; the reference contracts into a labelled source thumbnail and the opaque submission preview opens in contact with the work. Approved: the work moves 24px beneath the one lens on the stage, the approval rail, whose opaque backing reads Approved, Sep 10, 2026, Counter pour, Maya Chen, Loopday Coffee, Recorded example. Terms: the opaque terms open from the work's lower edge and US$75 with On approval arrives whole, with Approval earns, Ledger example unavailable and Payout is separate on the same plane. The work stays visible above the amount; the amount is never credited to Maya.

experiences.after_pass_2: The approval provenance wraps inside its opaque backing at phone width and carries Maya's name; the money block no longer repeats her approval; the source thumbnail sits 14px from the work and the submission preview is in edge contact with the carrier; the lime creator label is a neutral opaque strip; the navigation stays light through the whole inspection stage.
experiences.truth: US$75 is the reference opportunity's term, On approval. Counter pour is Maya Chen's own photograph, approved Sep 10, 2026, with no ledger record; the endpoint says Ledger example unavailable. Nothing is submitted, approved or credited by playback.
experiences.finishing: The transformation stays on one carrier. The approval is now a physical pass: the lens enters at the work's lower edge, sweeps up over it and settles inset from the top before the record reads. The terms come out from beneath the approved work rather than fading in beside it, and they share the work's end scale so the sheet stays flush with the frame. The work keeps as much of its size at the end as the stage allows (the scale and rise are computed from the stage height) instead of a fixed reduction. No text was added.

experiences.title: Drive sequence
experiences.body: The director's approved vehicle example, an oxblood estate wagon in a limestone courtyard, inside a fixed aperture. The photograph enters, the crop shifts closer without changing perspective (a scale of the whole plane: 1.22 on phone, 1.08 on desktop), the registered rear door zone reveals through a shutter with one leader to Rear doors, a coded Spurroom Bikes placement specimen travels from beside the car and is occluded by its registered on door counterpart beneath the photographed handle, the opaque campaign sheet opens attached to the photograph's right margin (below the aperture on phone), and its pre sized lower plane uncovers US$300 /month with Monthly approval. Placement preview lives on the one inspection lens at the aperture's corner; Vehicle example stays on its opaque tag throughout. The zone polygon, the specimen plane and the handle sample are stored in normalized coordinates against this exact asset and share the photograph's transform.

experiences.after_pass_2: Phone controls follow the active object (after the aperture in the first four beats, after the sheet in the last two) with no reserved gap; the phone rest state is the whole photograph, unshifted, with Vehicle example visible; the desktop campaign sheet is full size opaque paper revealed from its own edge with at most 48px of travel; the handle occlusion is confined to the handle and only present when the specimen is on the door; the phone sheet settles inline against the aperture without a floating shadow.
experiences.truth: The photograph is an illustrative vehicle example, not Eli's listing, an accepted vehicle or installed proof. Rear doors is the only supported placement group. The specimen is a Placement preview, never an installation. US$300 /month is the Spurroom Bikes campaign opportunity in Austin, Oct 1 to Dec 31, 2026, paid on monthly approved proof; Eli's US$240 asking rate is not shown here.
experiences.finishing: The placement is a decal on the real door, not an overlay: the specimen is mapped onto the door panel by a projective transform registered to the photograph (following the panel's slant and the wheel arch cut), the photograph's own paint is blended onto it so the door's shading and reflections carry across the decal, and its edge reads as vinyl. The rectangular handle occlusion is gone; the decal sits below the handle. The aperture is seated on the stage with a contact shadow. After the creative attaches, the camera pulls back: on desktop the aperture narrows from the right, the vehicle recedes to show the whole placement, and the campaign sheet opens in the freed column tied to the Rear doors row, so the sheet never covers the car; on phone the whole vehicle returns letterboxed and the sheet sits beneath the photograph, never over the wheels. The Vehicle example tag and the Placement preview lens step clear of the clipped bands. Steps and View campaign are reachable on every phone beat.

experiences.title: Business to Loyalty sequence
experiences.body: One relationship across three depths. Jasmine's typographic source marker (Joined from, Jasmine, Morning loop · Story campaign) is on the stage from the first frame and never enters a customer or Wallet object. The Loopday Story and its trusted campaign link are the campaign; Sara's recorded September 8 signup replay is the customer; the opaque member card concept (Apple, or Google through Wallet options) carries the dated returns September 8, 10, 13 and 16 and the labelled September 17 example continuation to Reward ready. Then the same marker advances onto the attribution datum and grows to 40 or 48px while the reward ready card is still in place; the card yields behind an opaque reading plane; and the three recorded aggregates open as ledges from the marker's underline: 4 Joined, 3 Came back, 1 Redeemed, whole values, no counter.

experiences.after_pass_2: The member identity, the dated event and the reward state are separate lines in a natural height band; the phone pass is 334px wide with Loopday Coffee readable; the desktop pass stays opaque and moves 360px right and 24px down behind the reading plane; the ledges sit on a 78px rhythm from the source datum; the source advances before the card yields.
experiences.truth: Public replay only: nothing joins, adds a visit, redeems or issues a pass. Sara's fifth visit is a labelled example continuation and no redemption is shown. The aggregates are the recorded fixture values; opening the loyalty preview shows its untouched 10, 6, 1, 2 baseline.
experiences.finishing: The close reconnects to the original campaign: the same Story creative that opened the chain returns beside the advanced Jasmine marker at attribution, so the finale reads campaign, source, dated returns, member card in one composition. The card yields whole beside the ledges on desktop and as a reduced card beneath them on phone, with no plane cutting through it. Nothing was turned into a chart.

paragraphs: Production build (next build with DESIGN_LAB=1, next start on port 3200), Lighthouse twice against the public homepage after the finishing pass, same procedure and machine class as the earlier rows.

Mobile first load media is 110KB over four images against 425KB over seven after the first build and 237KB over three in the current V3: the derivatives are AVIF, the business photograph is not requested on phone, and the Recreate work, the Drive vehicle and the Loyalty Story are requested only when their scene needs them. Desktop stays at 99 with LCP 0.9 s and zero layout shift; the mobile preset is 83 with LCP 4.5 s and 70 to 80 ms of blocking time. The mobile LCP did not move with the image weight: the largest contentful paint is the 47KB reference, and on the throttled preset the paint waits on the script and hydration, not on that file. The 2.5 s mobile target is still missed and is reported as missed.

Frame timing during native desktop scroll after the finishing pass: hero p50 16.7 ms, p95 33.4 ms, max 50 ms; Recreate p50 16.7, p95 33.3; Drive p50 16.7, p95 33.4, with 15 of 223 frames over 33 ms during the decal lighting and pull back; Loyalty p50 16.7, p95 16.8. No frame over 50 ms on any take.
performance.setup: Setup: next build with DESIGN_LAB=1 served by next start on port 3200; Lighthouse against HeadlessChrome 141 on the session's Linux container (benchmarkIndex 2312 to 2536 on these runs, 1689 on the V3 package runs, so this machine measured slightly faster); mobile preset is simulated slow 4G with 4x CPU throttling, desktop preset has no throttle. Accessibility stays at 98 for the same reason as before: the production root layout's skip link, outside this lab. Measured 2026-09-18.

sections.title: Fixed after the comparison
paragraphs: The director's comparison names four things it could see in the stills. Three were layering defects, not design questions, and were fixed after the comparison ran; the stills and recordings in this package are the recaptured ones, and the comparison text above describes the state before these fixes. No third director pass was run, per the brief's stop point.

Loyalty finale: the opaque plane that hid the ledges' overlap also cut through the card's label, brand and QR. The plane is gone. On desktop the whole card now yields to the right of the ledges; on tablet and phone it yields as a reduced card beside or beneath them, so Sara's card and Jasmine's advanced source stay visible together with a clean edge. The tablet source name, which the same check showed clipped at the left edge, is corrected with the same width as desktop.

Business hero: the campaign reference covered the heading of Maya's sheet, leaving only View person and Request. The sheet now sits in contact with the reference's lower edge with her name unobstructed.

Drive on phone: Steps and View campaign wrapped to a second row that the stage's fixed height clipped, so the phone showed the transport row only. The stage heights carry the second row on every beat.

Not changed: the Drive desktop still at the Monthly opportunity beat shows US$300 /month with Monthly approval and its qualification together (drive-d-0.94.png); the comparison judged this from a sampled strip frame between beats. The Drive specimen registration and the hero's supporting hierarchy are the director's remaining design notes and are left for the founder's decision.

sections.title: Generated supporting photography
paragraphs: The director wrote one media brief for this build, the vehicle placement photograph for Drive: an oxblood estate wagon at rest in a limestone courtyard, rear door and quarter panel clean for the placement zones, no lettering, no people. The image model rendered it and the director reviewed every round against its own brief. Three earlier runs were rejected, mostly for pixel count (the image API renders 3:2 at 1536x1024) and for edit artifacts; the pipeline now keeps every round beside its verdict and accepts a pixel count only objection. The approved round scored 9 of 10 on purpose, brand fit, professional finish, product correctness, not looking generated and premium feel, and 10 of 10 on being free of lettering. It is the only new photograph on the page. Every other image is an existing fixture with its binding unchanged.

sections.title: What is not built, on purpose
list: User Home, User Profile, Business Home, Business Loyalty and every other V3 surface are untouched. The brief limits this build to the public hero, Recreate, Drive and Business to Loyalty.
Nothing is migrated to production. The recomposition lives at /design-lab-v3 behind the DESIGN_LAB flag, on the working branch, unmerged.

No flow, copy rule, amount, state or truth binding changed. US$75 remains On approval for the Counter pour; the Latte take is the only recorded earnings example; Eli's US$240 listing and the Spurroom US$300 /month campaign are separate records; Jasmine has no portrait.
No fake 3D. The Drive moment is one photograph with coded layers: the aperture, the camera shift, the masked door zone, the specimen creative and the campaign sheet.
No third director pass. Two passes per experience were run and applied; the comparison below is the closing judgement, per the brief's stop point.
